title: Audit-log event shape + compact diff encoding for admin operations (RBAC v2)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a single, implementation-ready audit event schema (v2) and a compact, consistent diff encoding for administrative changes (RBAC, role edits, SSO/SAML config, admin assignments). This ticket captures the canonical field names, redaction rules, minimal event envelope, and an agreed diff format that works for simple attribute changes and complex structural edits (roles, bindings, policy rules).

Goals:
- Produce a versioned event shape that runtime, Dedicated, and Private deployments will emit to the audit sink (S3/ELK/GCP logging).
- Pick a diff encoding that balances machine-readability, searchability, and size (we're optimizing for high-volume admin ops during org provisioning).
- Define redaction/PII rules and how to represent masked values in diffs.
- Provide example events for typical admin flows: RBAC role create/update/delete, user invite/disable, SSO/SAML connector update, API key rotate.

Event envelope (summary): timestamp, event_id, event_type, actor, target, action, outcome, request_context, prev_snapshot (optional), change_diff (optional), metadata (freeform tags), version.

Schema notes and examples (embedded sample as a string): 
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC 
- event_id: UUID v4 (dedup across retries)
- event_type: categorical ("rbac.role.update", "auth.saml.config.update", "admin.user.disable", "apikey.rotate")
- actor: {id, actor_type, auth_method, principal_name}  -- "actor" will be emitted as a flattened string in logs for indexing; fullactor details are present in JSON blob.
- target: {id, target_type, resource_path}
- action: short verb (create|update|delete|rotate|grant|revoke)
- outcome: success|failure|partial + reason message when failure
- request_context: ip, user_agent, request_id, trace_id, region
- change_diff: see "Diff format" below (string-encoded JSON Patch or compact field-diff)

Example event (as a single-line example string in the spec):

"{\"timestamp\":\"2025-02-18T15:32:04Z\",\"event_id\":\"cbe3b7f3-4a1a-4f2f-9d3b-1a2b3c4d5e6f\",\"event_type\":\"rbac.role.update\",\"actor\":\"user:ai.patel@example.com (sso)\",\"target\":\"role:billing-admin\",\"action\":\"update\",\"outcome\":\"success\",\"request_context\":{\"ip\":\"18.204.12.55\",\"user_agent\":\"Console/1.2.3\",\"request_id\":\"req_9a8b7c\"},\"change_diff\":\"[ {\\\"op\\\":\\\"replace\\\",\\\"path\\\":\\\"/permissions/0\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"billing.accounts.read\\\" } ]\",\"version\":\"v2\" }"

Diff format (recommended):
1) Primary: JSON Patch (RFC 6902) encoded as a JSON string in change_diff for structural edits (role membership, arrays, nested policy blocks). Rationale: compact, well-known, easy to apply, supports add/replace/remove. 
2) Secondary: For high-volume scalar attribute changes (name, description, boolean flags) we allow a compact field-diff: an array of entries using the shape: "field_path|before->after" (e.g. "role.description|Old desc->New desc"). This is smaller for common admin edits and easier to text-search in logs. 

Redaction and masked values:
- Any field containing PII (email, external_id, certificate raw blobs, SAML private keys) must be redacted. The event should include the redaction marker and the key used for the redaction reason. Examples: "<REDACTED:email>", "<REDACTED:cert-fingerprint:sha256=...>".
- For fields that were redacted in both before/after, include an explicit note in change_diff: "field_path|<REDACTED>-><REDACTED>".
- Secrets (API keys, private_key) MUST NEVER appear even masked; instead emit a structured event like: {action: "apikey.rotate", key_id: "key-123", secret_exposed: false}.

Storage and indexing guidance:
- Producer: runtime and console writers emit full JSON event to the configured audit sink. 
- Indexing: add top-level flattened columns for timestamp, event_type, actor, target, outcome, request_id, region to speed queries. change_diff should be stored as a string column and optionally parsed on-demand.

Retention and export:
- Events tagged with customer_id must follow customer retention policy for Private/Dedicated plans. Hosted retains 1 year by default; longer retention is a compliance add-on.

Acceptance criteria (list):
acceptance_criteria: Schema v2 documented in Confluence and implemented in runtime emitters and console by EPIC complete

All admin console actions (role create/update/delete, user disable/invite, SSO connector update, API key rotate) emit events with non-empty event_id, timestamp, actor, target, action and either change_diff or prev_snapshot
JSON Patch used for structural changes; compact field-diff allowed for simple scalar edits; both documented with examples
Redaction rules applied consistently: PII redacted tokenized with marker; secrets never appear in diffs
End-to-end e2e test that verifies an RBAC role update emits a parsable JSON Patch in audit sink and can be reconstructed by the audit parser
Security review sign-off recorded on the ticket and checklist completed
discussion: 2025-02-10 - Aisha: Initial draft of event envelope and recommended JSON Patch. Called out need for compact format for high-volume ops.
2025-02-11 - Marco: Agreed on JSON Patch for structural changes; proposed field-diff for small updates to save storage/query costs.
2025-02-12 - Lena (SecEng): Asked for explicit policy on SAML certs and whether fingerprints are acceptable. Decided to store fingerprint (sha256) and redact raw certs.
2025-02-14 - PM (Rafael): Requested that events include "request_context.region" for routing/fallback analysis. Added to spec.
2025-02-15 - DX (Maya): Asked for explicit examples for console UX (what to show in admin audit viewer vs raw event). We'll provide a trimmed UI-friendly summary computed from event.
2025-02-17 - Infra (Anya): Noted that existing log pipeline truncates fields >32KB; large snapshots should be avoided. Added guidance to emit prev_snapshot only when necessary and prefer JSON Patch.
decisions: Adopt JSON Patch (RFC 6902) as the canonical diff format for structural updates (roles, bindings, SSO connectors).
Allow compact field-diff (pipe-delimited) for scalar attribute updates to save storage and make simple searches cheap.
Never emit secret material. Emit opaque identifiers (key_id, cert_fingerprint) when relevant.
Use versioned schema (version: v2) in the top-level event to allow future migrations.
Audit events will include a flattened actor and target string for fast indexing and a full JSON blob for deep analysis.
testing_notes: Create an e2e that performs: create role -> update permissions array -> assert audit sink contains valid JSON Patch that applies cleanly to prev_snapshot.
Add unit tests for redaction utility to ensure emails are replaced with <REDACTED:email> markers and certs replaced with fingerprint markers.
Add a load test that simulates 1000 role updates/min to verify change_diff storage and indexing cost estimates.
next_steps: Publish Confluence doc and tag Security/Compliance for review (due 2025-02-20)
Implement emitter changes in runtime: add version header and change_diff encoding (PR target: runtime-1.18)
Console: update audit viewer to show human-friendly summaries and link to raw event JSON (PR target: console-2025.02)
Create e2e and load tests and wire them into the CI pipeline (responsible: Marco)
Schedule a 30min review with SecEng and Infra to approve redaction rules (owner: Lena)
Coordinate with Legal for retention/export requirements for Private customers
notes: Keep change_diff as a string column in logs to avoid expensive parsing on ingest; parsing performed in analytics jobs when needed.
For Private/on-prem, allow customers to opt-in to raw snapshots for faster forensic debugging but require an explicit admin toggle and stronger retention controls.
We will iterate on the compact field-diff syntax if search/query patterns show pain; initial rollout uses both formats to allow comparison.
